value.rationale: A second-excited Hermite channel introduces two distinct interior zeros, creating a genuine simultaneous-covering design not present with two windows. The result identifies exact optimal second-order conditioning loss, strictly positive asymptotically necessary Gaussian and first-Hermite precision shares, and asymptotic rigidity for every optimizer. This is a natural sharp inversion design constant with practical mathematical implications for multichannel ambiguity deconvolution.
